notes.meaning: Jesus came back to Capernaum after traveling and preaching in nearby towns. Word spread quickly that He was staying at a house, which was likely Simon Peter's home. People were eager to see Him because of the miracles He had already done.

So many people crowded into the home that no one else could squeeze in, even by the doorway. Jesus used this moment to preach God's message to the gathering. His primary focus was always to share the good news, not just to draw crowds.
Four men arrived carrying a paralyzed man on a sleeping mat. The man was completely unable to walk or bring himself to Jesus. His friends showed great love by working together to carry him.

The crowd completely blocked the entrance, so the men climbed up to the flat roof. They dug through the clay and branches to make an opening right above Jesus. Then they carefully lowered their friend down into the room on his mat.

Jesus saw their active, bold trust in Him and spoke kindly to the paralyzed man. Instead of healing his legs first, Jesus told him his sins were forgiven. He took care of the man's deepest spiritual need before healing his body.

Some teachers of the law, called scribes, were sitting in the crowd watching Jesus closely. They did not say anything out loud yet, but they began arguing and complaining in their own minds. They were suspicious of Jesus and looked for reasons to criticize Him.

The scribes thought Jesus was speaking blasphemy, which means showing deep disrespect to God by claiming God's special rights. They knew from Scripture that God alone has the authority to forgive sins. Because they did not believe Jesus was God, they thought His words were an attack against the Lord.

Jesus instantly knew their silent thoughts through His divine knowledge. He directly asked them why they were questioning Him in their hearts. By uncovering their hidden thoughts, He showed that nothing was hidden from Him.

Jesus asked which statement was easier to make to a paralyzed man. Anyone can claim to forgive sins in secret because no one can see whether it really happened. Telling a paralyzed man to walk is harder to fake, because everyone can see if the miracle works.

Jesus called Himself the Son of Man, His chosen title that pointed to His role as the promised Savior. He decided to perform a visible miracle so the leaders would know His divine authority was real. His power to heal would prove He truly had the right to forgive sins on earth.
Jesus turned to the paralyzed man and gave him a clear command. He told him to stand up, pick up his sleeping mat, and walk home. This gave the man an immediate way to act on his faith.

The man jumped up right away, grabbed his mat, and walked out in full view of the whole crowd. The people were filled with awe and praised God for what had happened. They admitted they had never seen such miraculous power before.

Jesus walked out to the shore of the Sea of Galilee to find open space. A large crowd followed Him there, and He began teaching them God's truth. He gladly shared God's message wherever people were ready to listen.

As Jesus walked along, He saw Levi, who is also known as Matthew, collecting taxes at his toll booth. Most Jewish people despised tax collectors because they worked for the Roman rulers and often cheated the public. Jesus told Levi to follow Him, and Levi immediately left his wealthy job to become a disciple.

Levi hosted a dinner at his home to honor Jesus and introduce his friends to the Lord. Many other tax collectors and people known as open sinners sat down to eat with Jesus and His disciples. Many of these outcasts were drawn to Jesus and wanted to learn from Him.

Religious leaders who strictly kept Jewish customs noticed Jesus sharing a meal with these despised outcasts. In their culture, eating at the same table meant friendship and acceptance. They asked His disciples why their Master would associate with people of such poor reputation.

Jesus answered their complaint with a simple word picture about medical care. Healthy people do not need a doctor, but people who are sick do. He explained that His mission was not to cater to self-satisfied people who thought they were good enough, but to rescue sinners who knew they needed help.

The disciples of John the Baptist and the Pharisees regularly practiced fasting, which means going without food for a time to pray and mourn. People noticed that Jesus and His followers were enjoying meals instead. They came to ask why His disciples did not follow the same strict fasting habits.

Jesus compared His presence to a joyful wedding feast where He was the bridegroom. Wedding guests do not go without food and mourn while celebrating with the groom. As long as Jesus was with His followers, their time together was meant to be full of celebration.

Jesus warned that a dark time was coming when He would be taken away from them by suffering and death. Once the bridegroom was gone, His followers would have deep reasons to grieve and pray. In those days, fasting would fit their sorrow and their longing for Him.

Jesus gave an everyday example about clothing to show how things fit together. If someone sews a patch of new, unshrunk cloth onto an old garment, the new patch will shrink when washed and tear the weak fabric. The gospel of grace was not meant to be sewn like a small patch onto old legal ceremonies.

In those days, people kept drinks in animal skins that stretched as fresh grape juice fermented. Old wineskins became stiff and brittle, so pouring new wine into them would make them burst open and ruin everything. Jesus was showing that the new life and freedom of God's kingdom could not be forced into old religious rituals.

On the Jewish day of rest, called the Sabbath, Jesus and His disciples walked along paths through grainfields. Because the disciples were hungry, they began snapping off heads of wheat or barley and rubbing them in their hands to eat. Taking grain by hand from a neighbor's field was allowed by God's law.

Pharisees saw what happened and accused the disciples of breaking the Sabbath rules. The religious leaders had created extra human traditions that treated picking and rubbing grain as harvesting work. They blamed Jesus for allowing His followers to do what their traditions strictly forbade.

Jesus responded by asking if they had read what King David did in Scripture. When David and his men were running for their lives and starving, they had an urgent physical need. Jesus pointed to God's own word to answer their strict charges.

David entered the holy tent of worship during the era of high priest Abiathar and ate the special holy bread. By ceremonial law, that bread was set apart only for the priests to eat. Yet God did not condemn David, showing that meeting vital human needs matters more than strict ritual rules.

Jesus stated that God created the day of rest to bless and refresh human beings, not to make humans suffer under heavy burdens. Religious leaders had turned God's gift of rest into a harsh list of rules that crushed people. Any religious custom that harms people completely misses God's loving intent.

differ.view: Believers are still required to keep one full day out of seven holy as a moral day of rest, now observed on Sunday.
The Old Testament Sabbath commands were ceremonial laws fulfilled in Christ, freeing believers from binding Sabbath rules.

notes.meaning: Jesus concluded that the Son of Man has supreme authority even over the Sabbath day. Since He is the divine Lawgiver who established the day of rest, He alone has the right to decide how it should be kept. His followers can trust His mercy rather than human traditions.
